title: Pre-Analysis — Residual Fleet Position on the Initial Flight Deck Display Standard
abstract: Cancelled work order on the residual fleet still carrying the initial flight deck display standard. The configuration question turned out to belong to the avionics obsolescence board rather than to pre-analysis.

sections.objective: Establish how many aircraft still carry the initial flight deck display standard, what supporting them costs once the display supplier ends repair support at the end of the year, and whether the standard can be withdrawn from the spares catalogue without stranding those aircraft. The order was raised internally by avionics systems after a spares planning review flagged the last repair-capable shop.
sections.findings_summary: Two of the three findings were reached quickly and the third stopped the work. The initial standard is superseded by the rack and display replacement, and the replacement is a hard prerequisite relationship rather than an alternative, so the residual aircraft have exactly one forward route and it is not optional. The bulletin that installs the replacement is already open against most of them. The removal task still carries both standards, which is correct while the residual fleet exists and wrong the moment it does not. What stopped the order was scope: deciding whether to fund the residual retrofit, to negotiate extended repair support, or to accept dispatch under the minimum equipment list is a commercial and airworthiness judgement, not a configuration analysis, and it belongs to the obsolescence board.
sections.next_steps: Hand the residual fleet decision to the avionics obsolescence board with the configuration picture attached. Recommend that whatever it decides is executed through the existing rack replacement bulletin rather than through a new one, since that bulletin is already open on most of the affected aircraft. Do not re-raise this work order; reopen the documentation actions only once the board has a position.

similarity_seeds: last repair capable shop for a flight deck display unit
residual fleet on a superseded avionics standard

tasks.title: Establish the residual fleet still on the initial display standard
Confirm the forward configuration route and its prerequisites
Cost extended repair support against residual retrofit

expected_findings.rationale: The rack and display replacement supersedes the initial standard and is the only forward route for the residual aircraft. It is not an optional improvement they can decline, which is how the spares planning review had understood it.
expected_findings.resolution: State the single forward route in the residual fleet paper handed to the obsolescence board.

expected_findings.rationale: The replacement bulletin is already open against most of the residual aircraft with an effectivity that assumes an unhurried retrofit. Ending repair support turns it into a time-limited action and the wording does not reflect that.
expected_findings.resolution: Recommend re-issuing the bulletin with a compliance date once the board has decided, rather than opening a new bulletin.

expected_findings.rationale: The removal task carries both display standards, which is correct while the residual fleet exists. It becomes dead content the moment the last aircraft is converted, and nobody owns the trigger to remove it.
expected_findings.resolution: Attach the content withdrawal to the last-aircraft milestone in the board decision rather than to a date.

type_data.conclusion: Cancelled. The configuration picture was complete after two weeks; the funding and airworthiness judgement that follows from it is not a pre-analysis decision and was delegated to the avionics obsolescence board.
